name: Dark Pink
lede: Dark Pink darkens [[pink]] toward magenta, and despite the plainness of its name it is one of the rarest colors in our entire painting archive, matched in just two of 23,781 paintings.

sections.title: A darkened pink
sections.body:
Dark Pink applies our modifier grammar's dark to [[pink]], whose own name comes from the flower, not the other way round: *pinks* were a garden flower (Dianthus) centuries before pink named a color in English [1]. The parent entry here was crowdsourced in the 2010 xkcd color survey, where thousands of people were simply shown a swatch and asked to type a name for it [1].

Its closest measured match is [[ruber]], only 2.6 units away and nearly the same color; [[telemagenta]] and [[cerise]] are both a touch more vivid, and [[razzmatazz]] sits a little further off at 4.1 units, also more vivid [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is one of the rarest matches in our archive: it covers at least five per cent of the canvas in only 2 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.01 per cent, as photographed [3]. Both matches date to the 1900s, roughly fourteen times that century's rate for the rest of the archive combined [3]. One of the two, an untitled Indian figure study, carries it over nearly 30 per cent of the canvas, far more than most matches of any color manage [3]. As photographed: these are computed color matches on museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not a pigment test [3].
